_comment: What the aliases published under our own domains were verified to be, and why each is recorded.
Checked by tools/check-dns-exposure.py --baseline dns-baseline.json, which runs this product's
own alias_takeover module and fails only on a regression: an alias worse than the one recorded
here, or a new bad one that was not. The known-and-recorded state does not fail the build,
because a permanently red gate for a reason the author of an unrelated pull request cannot act
on is a gate people learn to click past.
resolves             the destination resolves to an address
no_address           the destination exists but publishes no address record
dangling             the destination does not exist; whether it is claimable is unproven
claimable_service    the destination does not exist and its parent hands out names on request
unregistered_domain  no part of the destination is registered; the domain itself is available
A verdict of 'unresolved' is none of these. It means the resolver's negative answers could not
be trusted, so nothing was measured — the check reports that and exits 2 rather than passing.
Only aliases worth recording are listed. An alias whose destination resolves is the normal case
and is not enumerated here; the check treats an unlisted alias as expected-to-resolve, so a new
alias that does NOT resolve fails the gate the first time it appears. That is the point.
Tighten an entry the moment its record improves — an improvement is reported, not silently
accepted, precisely so the gain gets held.

note: LIVE AND OPEN. The destination is NXDOMAIN and its parent mynetgear.com is served by
ns2.no-ip.com, a self-service dynamic-DNS provider where an unregistered name is claimed
by whoever asks for it first. Whoever claims 'icit' there controls what vpn.ironcityit.com
answers — on a hostname staff and clients are taught to trust, with a certificate that
Recorded rather than fixed because the fix is a DNS change on ironcityit.com, which is not
this repository's to make and needs a person: delete the record, or re-claim the
destination. Deleting is the safer order.
It is recorded at its true severity so that the gate is honest about the starting point
and still fires if it gets worse, or if a second one appears.
